beige.explanation: "Beige" means "beige", a light, sandy color like dry sand.

sentence.da: Sandet på stranden er **beige**.
sentence.en: The sand on the beach is beige.

bekendt.explanation: "Bekendt" means "familiar" or "known". The same word is also a person: "en bekendt" (an acquaintance) is someone you know only slightly, not a close friend.

sentence.da: Hendes stemme lyder **bekendt**.
sentence.en: Her voice sounds familiar.

bekvem.explanation: "Bekvem" means "convenient" or "comfortable", but it is often used about easy solutions: "en bekvem undskyldning" (a convenient excuse). For a comfortable chair, Danes say "behagelig" (pleasant): "en behagelig stol" (a comfortable chair).

sentence.da: Det er en **bekvem** måde at betale på.
sentence.en: It is a convenient way to pay.

bekymrende.explanation: "Bekymrende" means "worrying": it describes the thing that makes you worried. The person who feels it is "bekymret" (worried): "Jeg er bekymret" (I am worried).

sentence.da: Det er **bekymrende**, at så mange unge sover for lidt.
sentence.en: It is worrying that so many young people sleep too little.

belysning.explanation: "Belysning" means "lighting": the lamps and light that make a place bright, in a room or on a street. It can also mean that a subject is examined: "en belysning af sagen" (a closer look at the matter).

sentence.da: God **belysning** i gaden gør os trygge, når det er mørkt.
sentence.en: Good lighting in the street makes us feel safe when it is dark.

bemærkelsesværdig.explanation: "Bemærkelsesværdig" means "remarkable", worth noticing: "et bemærkelsesværdigt resultat" (a remarkable result). It is built from at bemærke (to notice) and værdig (worthy).

sentence.da: Hendes udholdenhed er **bemærkelsesværdig**, når man tænker på hendes alder.
sentence.en: Her stamina is remarkable when you think of her age.

benzin.explanation: "Benzin" means "gasoline", which Americans often call gas. A diesel car needs diesel instead.

sentence.da: Min bil kører på **benzin**, ikke på diesel.
sentence.en: My car runs on gasoline, not on diesel.

beredvillighed.explanation: "En beredvillighed" means "a readiness", being quick and glad to help others.

sentence.da: Når man gerne og hurtigt hjælper, viser man **beredvillighed**.
sentence.en: When you help gladly and quickly, you show readiness.

berettiget.explanation: "Berettiget" means "justified": it has good reasons behind it. It also means "entitled": allowed to receive something: "Du er berettiget til hjælp" (You are entitled to help).

sentence.da: Hendes kritik var **berettiget**, fordi fejlen var tydelig.
sentence.en: Her criticism was justified because the mistake was obvious.

beruset.explanation: "Beruset" means "drunk" or "intoxicated". It is the formal word used in police reports and news, such as "en beruset bilist" (an intoxicated driver). In everyday speech Danes say "fuld" (drunk): "Han er fuld" (He is drunk).

sentence.da: Det er forbudt at køre bil, når man er **beruset**.
sentence.en: It is forbidden to drive a car when you are drunk.

berømt.explanation: "Berømt" means "famous". To say what someone or something is famous for, put "for" after it: "Den er berømt for sin ost" (It is famous for its cheese).

sentence.da: Hun er en **berømt** sanger i hele landet.
sentence.en: She is a famous singer all over the country.

beskadiget.explanation: "Beskadiget" means "damaged", for something that has been harmed but is not necessarily broken: "Pakken er beskadiget" (The package is damaged).

sentence.da: Bilen er **beskadiget** efter ulykken.
sentence.en: The car is damaged after the accident.

beskeden.explanation: "Beskeden" means "modest" and describes someone who does not brag. It is also used for a small amount: "en beskeden løn" (a modest salary).

sentence.da: Hun er **beskeden** og snakker aldrig om sine succeser.
sentence.en: She is modest and never talks about her successes.

beskidt.explanation: "Beskidt" means "dirty", covered in dirt or mud.

sentence.da: Man bliver **beskidt** af at lege i mudder.
sentence.en: You get dirty from playing in mud.

beskyttelse.explanation: "Beskyttelse" means "protection", something that keeps you safe from harm.

sentence.da: Solcreme giver **beskyttelse** mod solen.
sentence.en: Sunscreen gives protection from the sun.

beskyttende.explanation: "Beskyttende" means "protective". It describes things that keep harm away, such as "en beskyttende hjelm" (a protective helmet), and people who watch over someone: "en beskyttende far" (a protective father). It comes from "at beskytte" (to protect).

sentence.da: Han bruger **beskyttende** briller, når han saver i træ.
sentence.en: He uses protective goggles when he saws wood.

beslutsomhed.explanation: "En beslutsomhed" means "a determination", acting firmly without doubt once your mind is made up. It describes how a person acts, unlike "en beslutning" (a decision), which is the decision itself.

sentence.da: Hun tøvede ikke, men handlede med **beslutsomhed**.
sentence.en: She did not hesitate but acted with determination.

beslægtet.explanation: "Beslægtet" means "related" in the family sense: "Er I beslægtede?" (Are you two related?). It is also used for languages and words that come from the same origin.

sentence.da: Ulven er tæt **beslægtet** med vores hunde.
sentence.en: The wolf is closely related to our dogs.

bestemt.explanation: "Bestemt" means "for sure" and "certain", in two uses. To stress a statement it means "for sure": "Hun kommer bestemt" (She is coming for sure). To point at one particular thing it means "certain": "en bestemt bog" (a certain book).

forms.en: I definitely do not want to

sentence.da: Det er **bestemt** en god idé.
sentence.en: That is definitely a good idea.

bestemt form.explanation: "En bestemt form" means "a form with the", the version of a word that says "the". Danish usually puts "the" on the end of the word instead of in front: "en hund" (a dog) becomes "hunden" (the dog), and "et hus" (a house) becomes "huset" (the house).

sentence.da: Ordet bilen er i **bestemt form**, men en bil er det ikke.
sentence.en: The word bilen is in the definite form, but en bil is not.

bestik.explanation: "Bestik" means "cutlery": the knives, forks and spoons you eat with. For a single piece, say "en kniv" (a knife), "en gaffel" (a fork) or "en ske" (a spoon).

sentence.da: Jeg lægger **bestik** og tallerkener på bordet.
sentence.en: I put cutlery and plates on the table.

bestikkelse.explanation: "En bestikkelse" means "a bribe", money or a gift given to someone in power to get an unfair favor. Without "en", it names the crime: "Han blev anklaget for bestikkelse" (He was accused of bribery).

sentence.da: Politiet mener, at manden tog imod **bestikkelse** fra firmaet.
sentence.en: The police believe the man took bribes from the company.

besvær.explanation: "Et besvær" means "trouble" or "a hassle", the effort or inconvenience that something costs you. It is also part of a polite phrase: "Undskyld besværet" (Sorry for the trouble), said after you have asked someone for something.

sentence.da: Det er for meget **besvær** at rejse så langt for et møde.
sentence.en: It is too much trouble to travel so far for a meeting.

besværlig.explanation: "Besværlig" means "troublesome", costing a lot of effort. It also describes a person who is awkward to deal with: "en besværlig kunde" (a demanding customer).

sentence.da: Vejen til hytten er **besværlig**, fordi den er stejl og mudret.
sentence.en: The road to the cabin is troublesome because it is steep and muddy.

beton.explanation: "Beton" means "concrete", the hard gray building material. It is the finished material, while "cement" (cement) is only the powder it is made from. You say "beton" with no "en": "Der er beton overalt" (There is concrete everywhere).

sentence.da: Gulvet i kælderen er lavet af **beton**.
sentence.en: The floor in the basement is made of concrete.

betydelig.explanation: "Betydelig" means "significant", mostly in the sense of large in amount or degree: "en betydelig stigning" (a considerable rise). To say that something has great meaning, use "betydningsfuld" (full of meaning).

sentence.da: Hun har en **betydelig** indflydelse på beslutningen.
sentence.en: She has a significant influence on the decision.

betydningsfuld.explanation: "Betydningsfuld" means "significant", full of meaning and weight, built from betydning (meaning) and fuld (full). You use it when something matters a lot: "en betydningsfuld opdagelse" (a significant discovery). Do not mix it up with "betydelig" (considerable), which says something is large in amount: "en betydelig stigning" (a considerable rise).

sentence.da: Opfindelsen af trykpressen var en **betydningsfuld** begivenhed i historien.
sentence.en: The invention of the printing press was a significant event in history.

betænkelig.explanation: "Betænkelig" means "doubtful" or "worrying", for something that makes you uneasy about whether it is wise or safe.

sentence.da: Situationen er **betænkelig**, fordi floden stiger hurtigt.
sentence.en: The situation is worrying because the river is rising fast.

bevidst.explanation: "Bevidst" means "conscious" or "deliberate". About an act it means that it was done with intent: "Hun gjorde det bevidst" (She did it on purpose). With "om" (about), it means aware of something: "bevidst om faren" (aware of the danger).

sentence.da: Han er **bevidst** om, at det kan være farligt.
sentence.en: He is aware that it can be dangerous.

bevidsthed.explanation: "Bevidsthed" means "consciousness", both being awake and being aware of something. To say someone passes out, use "at miste bevidstheden" (to lose consciousness).

sentence.da: Efter ulykken kom han til **bevidsthed** igen.
sentence.en: After the accident he regained consciousness.

bevidstløs.explanation: "Bevidstløs" means "unconscious", not awake and not reacting, for example after a fall. The ending "løs" means "without", as in "hjælpeløs" (helpless).

sentence.da: Efter faldet lå cyklisten **bevidstløs** på vejen.
sentence.en: After the fall the cyclist lay unconscious on the road.

bevismateriale.explanation: "Et bevismateriale" means "evidence", all the documents, photos and recordings collected to show what happened in a case.

sentence.da: Fotos, breve og optagelser er alt sammen **bevismateriale** i en retssag.
sentence.en: Photos, letters and recordings are all evidence in a trial.

bevæbnet.explanation: "Bevæbnet" means "armed", carrying something to fight with. Add "med" (with) to name the weapon: "Han er bevæbnet med en kniv" (He is armed with a knife).

sentence.da: Politiet sagde, at manden var **bevæbnet** med en kniv.
sentence.en: The police said that the man was armed with a knife.

beæret.explanation: "Beæret" means "honored", feeling that someone has shown you great respect. Add "over" (about) to give the reason: "Jeg er beæret over invitationen" (I am honored by the invitation).

sentence.da: Hun følte sig **beæret**, da kongen takkede hende personligt.
sentence.en: She felt honored when the king thanked her personally.

bifald.explanation: "Et bifald" means "applause", the sound an audience makes to show it liked something. It is also used for "approval" of an idea or decision: "Forslaget fik bifald" (The proposal got approval).

sentence.da: Efter koncerten fik orkestret et langt **bifald** fra publikum.
sentence.en: After the concert, the orchestra got long applause from the audience.

billedkunst.explanation: "Billedkunst" means "art", the school subject where pupils draw, paint and make pictures.

sentence.da: I **billedkunst** lærer børnene at tegne og male.
sentence.en: In art, the children learn to draw and paint.

billig.explanation: "Billig" means "cheap", costing little. It can also sound negative, as if the thing is poorly made: "Jakken ser billig ud" (The jacket looks cheap). In a shop you can ask: "Har du noget billigere?" (Do you have something cheaper?)

sentence.da: Maden er **billig**, kun tyve kroner.
sentence.en: The food is cheap, only twenty kroner.

biodiversitet.explanation: "Biodiversitet" means "biodiversity", the variety of living things in one place. A forest with many kinds of plants and animals has a lot of it, while a field with a single crop has little.

sentence.da: Skoven har stor **biodiversitet**, fordi der lever mange forskellige arter.
sentence.en: The forest has great biodiversity because many different species live there.

biologi.explanation: "Biologi" means "biology", the study of plants, animals and the human body. To say you are good at it, use "til" (at): "Jeg er god til biologi" (I am good at biology).

sentence.da: Vi lærer om dyr og planter i **biologi**.
sentence.en: We learn about animals and plants in biology.

biologisk.explanation: "Biologisk" means "biological", about living things and the science of them. It is also used for family by birth, as in "biologiske forældre" (biological parents), as opposed to adoptive ones.

sentence.da: **Biologisk** affald er rester af planter og dyr.
sentence.en: Biological waste is what is left of plants and animals.

bitter.explanation: "Bitter" means "bitter", the taste of strong coffee. It also describes a person who stays angry about something that happened: "Hun er bitter" (She is bitter).

sentence.da: Kaffen er for **bitter** for mig.
sentence.en: The coffee is too bitter for me.

blandet.explanation: "Blandet" means "mixed" and is used for things made of different kinds, such as "en blandet salat" (a mixed salad). It is also used for feelings: "blandede følelser" (mixed feelings).

sentence.da: Jeg køber **blandet** slik til børnene.
sentence.en: I buy mixed candy for the kids.

blandt.explanation: "Blandt" means "among": "Han er blandt de bedste" (He is among the best). For just two things, use "mellem" (between): "mellem huset og træet" (between the house and the tree).

sentence.da: Katten gemmer sig **blandt** blomsterne.
sentence.en: The cat hides among the flowers.

blandt andet.explanation: "Blandt andet" means "among other things". Say it when you name one example out of several: "Vi talte blandt andet om prisen" (We talked about the price, among other things). In writing it is shortened to "bl.a."

forms.da: Vi talte blandt andet om musik.
forms.en: We talked about music, among other things.
She can swim, among other things.

sentence.da: Jeg købte **blandt andet** brød og ost.
sentence.en: I bought bread and cheese, among other things.

blank.explanation: "Blank" means "shiny": "en blank overflade" (a shiny surface). It can also describe a page with nothing on it: "et blankt ark" (a blank sheet).

sentence.da: Bilen er **blank**, fordi jeg har vasket den.
sentence.en: The car is shiny because I washed it.

bleg.explanation: "Bleg" means "pale", for a face or skin that has lost its color, such as from illness, fear or cold. It also describes washed-out colors: "blege farver" (pale colors).

sentence.da: Hun blev helt **bleg** i ansigtet, da hun hørte nyheden.
sentence.en: She turned completely pale in the face when she heard the news.

blind.explanation: "Blind" means "blind", for someone who cannot see.

sentence.da: Han er **blind** og kan ikke se.
sentence.en: He is blind and cannot see.

blod.explanation: "Blod" means "blood". It is the first part of many longer words: "blodprøve" (blood test) and "blodtryk" (blood pressure).

sentence.da: Lægen tager en prøve af mit **blod**.
sentence.en: The doctor takes a sample of my blood.

blodig.explanation: "Blodig" means "bloody", covered in blood or full of violence.

sentence.da: Han fik en **blodig** næse, da bolden ramte ham.
sentence.en: He got a bloody nose when the ball hit him.

blodsukker.explanation: "Blodsukker" means "blood sugar", the amount of sugar in your blood. People with diabetes check it often with a small device, to see whether they need food or medicine.

sentence.da: Efter et stort måltid stiger mit **blodsukker**.
sentence.en: After a big meal my blood sugar rises.

blodtryk.explanation: "Et blodtryk" means "blood pressure", how hard your blood pushes against the walls of the vessels in your body. Doctors often check it, because a value that is too high can strain the heart.

sentence.da: Lægen måler mit **blodtryk** med en manchet om overarmen.
sentence.en: The doctor measures my blood pressure with a cuff around the upper arm.

blokeret.explanation: "Blokeret" means "blocked", when something is in the way or shut, so nothing can get through. It is also used for a bank card or account that has been stopped, often after a theft: "Dit kort er blokeret" (Your card is blocked).

sentence.da: Vejen er **blokeret** af et væltet træ.
sentence.en: The road is blocked by a fallen tree.

blomkål.explanation: "Blomkål" means "cauliflower". It is built from blomst (flower) and kål (cabbage), so it literally means "flower cabbage".

sentence.da: **Blomkål** er hvid og ligner en lille blomst.
sentence.en: Cauliflower is white and looks like a small flower.

blond.explanation: "Blond" means "blond", a light yellow hair color: "blondt hår" (blond hair), "en blond kvinde" (a blond woman).

sentence.da: Min søster er **blond**, men jeg har mørkt hår.
sentence.en: My sister is blond, but I have dark hair.

blot.explanation: "Blot" means "merely" or "just". It also appears in wishes: "Havde jeg blot vidst det!" (If only I had known!).

forms.en: He is only ten years old.

sentence.da: Jeg ville **blot** sige tak.
sentence.en: I just wanted to say thanks.

bly.explanation: "Et bly" means "lead", the heavy, soft, gray metal.

sentence.da: Gamle rør kan være lavet af **bly**, som er giftigt.
sentence.en: Old pipes can be made of lead, which is poisonous.

blå.explanation: "Blå" means "blue". Put "lyse" (light) or "mørke" (dark) in front to make shades: "lyseblå" means "light blue" and "mørkeblå" means "dark blue".

sentence.da: Himlen er **blå** i dag.
sentence.en: The sky is blue today.

blæsende.explanation: "Blæsende" means "windy", with strong wind blowing. It comes from "at blæse" (to blow). To say it is windy right now, use "Det blæser" (It is windy).

sentence.da: Det var en **blæsende** dag ved havet.
sentence.en: It was a windy day by the sea.

blæst.explanation: "Blæst" means "wind", the windy weather you feel outdoors.

sentence.da: Der er meget **blæst** på stranden i dag.
sentence.en: There is a lot of wind on the beach today.

blød.explanation: "Blød" means "soft", pleasant to touch. It also describes a quiet, gentle sound: "en blød stemme" (a soft voice).

sentence.da: Jeg sover godt i en **blød** seng.
sentence.en: I sleep well in a soft bed.

blødende.explanation: "Blødende" means "bleeding", for a person or a body part that is losing blood right now. It comes from "at bløde" (to bleed).

sentence.da: Pres på det **blødende** sted, indtil blødningen stopper.
sentence.en: Press on the bleeding spot until the bleeding stops.

bogstavelig talt.explanation: "Bogstavelig talt" means "literally", used when something is really true as said, not as a figure of speech. The opposite is "billedligt talt" (figuratively speaking).

sentence.da: Der var **bogstavelig talt** ingen mennesker på gaden, ikke en eneste.
sentence.en: There were literally no people in the street, not a single one.

bogstaveligt.explanation: "Bogstaveligt" means "literally", exactly as the words say, with no hidden meaning. It usually comes after "at forstå" (to understand) or "at tage" (to take): "at tage noget bogstaveligt" (to take something literally).

forms.da: Du skal ikke tage det bogstaveligt

sentence.da: Små børn forstår ofte ord **bogstaveligt**, så ironi er svær for dem.
sentence.en: Small children often understand words literally, so irony is hard for them.

boligmarkedet.explanation: "Boligmarkedet" means "the housing market", the buying, selling and renting of apartments and houses, with the prices that go with it.

sentence.da: Priserne på **boligmarkedet** er steget meget i København.
sentence.en: Prices on the housing market have risen a lot in Copenhagen.

boligstøtte.explanation: "En boligstøtte" means "housing benefit", money from the state that helps people with a low income pay for where they live. It comes in two forms: "boligsikring" (housing benefit for most people) and "boligydelse" (housing benefit for pensioners).

sentence.da: Staten giver **boligstøtte** til folk med lav indkomst og dyr husleje.
sentence.en: The state gives housing benefit to people with a low income and expensive rent.

boller i karry.explanation: "Boller i karry" means "meatballs in curry sauce", a classic Danish home-cooked dish of small balls of minced meat in a mild curry sauce. Here "boller" means meatballs, not the sweet buns that are also called "boller".

forms.en: meatballs in curry sauce with rice
a portion of meatballs in curry sauce

sentence.da: Jeg laver **boller i karry** af hakket svinekød og serverer dem med ris.
sentence.en: I make meatballs in curry sauce from minced pork and serve them with rice.

bomuld.explanation: "Bomuld" means "cotton", the soft fiber from the cotton plant, used for T-shirts and towels.

sentence.da: Man dyrker **bomuld** i varme lande og laver tøj af det.
sentence.en: Cotton is grown in warm countries and clothes are made from it.

borgerservice.explanation: "Borgerservice" means "Citizen Services": the municipal office for practical matters like a health insurance card, a passport or registering your address. It is written with a capital B, like the name of an office.

forms.en: I have to go to Citizen Services.

sentence.da: Jeg skal have nyt pas på **Borgerservice**.
sentence.en: I need a new passport at Citizen Services.

bortset fra.explanation: "Bortset fra" means "apart from" or "except". It introduces the exception to what you just said: "Alle kom, bortset fra Anna" (Everyone came, except Anna).

sentence.da: Alle kom **bortset fra** Lars.
sentence.en: Everyone came except Lars.

bravo.explanation: "Bravo" means "bravo" and is the same word as in English. Shout it to praise a performance or a good effort.

sentence.da: **Bravo**, det var en flot koncert!
sentence.en: Bravo, that was a great concert!

bred.explanation: "Bred" means "wide" or "broad", for how far something stretches from side to side: a road, a river, a smile.

sentence.da: Vejen er **bred**, ikke smal.
sentence.en: The road is wide, not narrow.

briller.explanation: "Briller" means "glasses" (for your eyes). It always ends in "r", even for one pair: "Jeg har nye briller" (I have new glasses). To say you are wearing them, use "at have briller på" (to have glasses on).

sentence.da: Jeg kan ikke læse uden mine **briller**.
sentence.en: I cannot read without my glasses.

brint.explanation: "Brint" means "hydrogen", the lightest gas there is. It is also used as a clean fuel for cars and buses, since burning it gives only water.

sentence.da: Vand består af ilt og **brint**.
sentence.en: Water consists of oxygen and hydrogen.

britisk.explanation: "Britisk" means "British", from Great Britain. Do not mix it up with "engelsk" (English), which is about England and the English language.

sentence.da: Han bor i London og er **britisk**.
sentence.en: He lives in London and is British.

broccoli.explanation: "Broccoli" means "broccoli", a green vegetable with a thick stalk and many small tops.

sentence.da: **Broccoli** er grøn og ligner et lille træ.
sentence.en: Broccoli is green and looks like a little tree.

brugbar.explanation: "Brugbar" means "usable" or "useful", for something that works well enough for the job: "et brugbart forslag" (a usable suggestion). Do not mix it up with "nyttig" (helpful), which you say about something that helps you a lot: "en nyttig tip" (a helpful tip).

sentence.da: Cyklen er gammel, men den er stadig **brugbar**.
sentence.en: The bike is old, but it is still usable.

brugt.explanation: "Brugt" means "used" or "secondhand", for things that someone owned before you. It comes from "at bruge" (to use).

sentence.da: Jeg købte en **brugt** cykel på nettet.
sentence.en: I bought a used bike online.

brun.explanation: "Brun" means "brown". It is also used for a suntan: "Du er blevet brun" (You have gotten a tan).

sentence.da: Chokolade er **brun**, ikke hvid.
sentence.en: Chocolate is brown, not white.

brunede kartofler.explanation: "Brunede kartofler" means "caramelized potatoes", small boiled potatoes turned in caramel until they are golden and sweet. They are a traditional side dish for the Christmas roast.

sentence.da: Til julemaden laver vi **brunede kartofler** med sukker og smør.
sentence.en: For the Christmas meal we make caramelized potatoes with sugar and butter.

brutal.explanation: "Brutal" means "brutal", for violence that is harsh and cruel. It is also used for honesty that is blunt and painful, as in "brutal ærlighed" (brutal honesty).

sentence.da: Filmen var **brutal**, og mange vendte blikket væk.
sentence.en: The film was brutal, and many looked away.

brændende.explanation: "Brændende" means "burning", something that is alight right now. It is also used for strong feelings and urgent matters: "et brændende ønske" (a burning wish).

sentence.da: De hentede børnene ud af det **brændende** hus og slukkede ilden.
sentence.en: They got the children out of the burning house and put out the fire.

brændstof.explanation: "Brændstof" means "fuel", for example for a car. It is built from brænde (to burn) and stof (material), and the same "stof" is in "et sprængstof" (an explosive).

sentence.da: Bilen bruger meget **brændstof** på motorvejen.
sentence.en: The car uses a lot of fuel on the highway.

brød.explanation: "Brød" means "bread". To say how many loaves, put the number before "brød" and leave the word unchanged: "to brød" (two loaves).

sentence.da: Jeg køber **brød** hos bageren.
sentence.en: I buy bread at the baker's.

buddhisme.explanation: "Buddhisme" means "Buddhism", the religion based on the teachings of Buddha. Danish writes it with a lowercase b, while English writes Buddhism with an uppercase B.

sentence.da: I **buddhisme** er meditation en vigtig del af livet.
sentence.en: In Buddhism, meditation is an important part of life.

bukser.explanation: "Bukser" means "pants" or "trousers". It always ends in "r", even for one pair, so you count pairs: "to par bukser" (two pairs of pants).

sentence.da: Jeg har **bukser** og sko på.
sentence.en: I am wearing pants and shoes.

bulgur.explanation: "Bulgur" means "bulgur", cracked wheat that is boiled until soft.

sentence.da: Jeg laver en salat af **bulgur**, tomat og persille.
sentence.en: I make a salad of bulgur, tomato and parsley.

buttet.explanation: "Buttet" means "chubby", pleasantly soft and full, mostly about babies and small children. About an adult it can sound unkind.

sentence.da: Den lille baby er **buttet**, og hans arme er bløde.
sentence.en: The little baby is chubby, and his arms are soft.

bydemåde.explanation: "En bydemåde" means "imperative", the form of a word you use to give an order or make a request, like "Kom her!" (Come here!) or "Hjælp mig!" (Help me!). The word literally means "ordering way", from byde (to order) and måde (way).

sentence.da: Sætningen Luk døren! står i **bydemåde**.
sentence.en: The sentence Close the door! is in the imperative.

byg.explanation: "Et byg" means "barley", a grain used for animal feed and for "byggryn" (pearl barley). "Byg!" is also the command "Build!", from "at bygge" (to build).

sentence.da: Man bruger **byg** til at lave øl.
sentence.en: Barley is used to make beer.

byplanlægning.explanation: "Byplanlægning" means "urban planning", deciding how a town or city grows: where roads, buildings and green areas go. It is built from by (town) and planlægning (planning).

sentence.da: God **byplanlægning** gør det let at gå og cykle i byen.
sentence.en: Good urban planning makes it easy to walk and bike in the city.

byttepenge.explanation: "Byttepenge" means "change", the money you get back when you pay more than the price. Like "penge" (money), it has no article in front: "Her er dine byttepenge" (Here is your change). It comes from "at bytte" (to exchange).

sentence.da: Du får 20 kroner i **byttepenge**.
sentence.en: You get 20 kroner in change.

både…og.explanation: "Både … og" means "both … and", with "både" at the start and "og" in the middle: "Det er både billigt og godt" (It is both cheap and good).

forms.da: både i dag og i morgen

sentence.da: Hun taler **både** dansk **og** engelsk.
sentence.en: She speaks both Danish and English.

bærbar.explanation: "Bærbar" means "portable", something you can carry. You can also name the laptop with just "en bærbar": "Jeg har købt en ny bærbar" (I bought a new laptop).

sentence.da: Min computer er **bærbar** og let at tage med.
sentence.en: My computer is portable and easy to take along.

bæredygtig.explanation: "Bæredygtig" means "sustainable", something that can continue without using up nature's resources. The word literally means "able to carry", from bære (carry) and dygtig (able).

sentence.da: En **bæredygtig** løsning kan holde i mange år uden at ødelægge naturen.
sentence.en: A sustainable solution can last for many years without destroying nature.

bæredygtighed.explanation: "Bæredygtighed" means "sustainability", the idea of living and producing without using up what nature gives. To describe a choice or a product, use "bæredygtig" (sustainable): "en bæredygtig løsning" (a sustainable solution).

sentence.da: Eleverne lærer om **bæredygtighed** og om at passe på naturen.
sentence.en: The students learn about sustainability and about taking care of nature.

bønner.explanation: "Bønner" means "beans". It also means "prayers" (from "en bøn", a prayer): "Mine bønner blev hørt" (My prayers were heard). A sentence about food or cooking means beans.

sentence.da: Jeg spiser **bønner** og majs til aftensmad.
sentence.en: I eat beans and corn for dinner.

børnepasning.explanation: "Børnepasning" means "childcare", looking after small children during the day while adults work. In Denmark the municipality arranges and partly pays for it.

sentence.da: Vi har brug for **børnepasning**, fordi begge forældre arbejder.
sentence.en: We need childcare because both parents work.

en baby.explanation: "En baby" means "a baby", someone only a few months or a year old.

sentence.da: Vores **baby** er to måneder gammel.
sentence.en: Our baby is two months old.

en babyalarm.explanation: "En babyalarm" means "a baby monitor", a device with two parts: a microphone by the baby and a receiver for the parents.

sentence.da: Med en **babyalarm** kan vi høre barnet, når vi er i stuen.
sentence.en: With a baby monitor we can hear the child when we are in the living room.

en babysitter.explanation: "En babysitter" means "a babysitter", someone who stays with kids for an evening.

sentence.da: En **babysitter** passer børnene, når vi er ude.
sentence.en: A babysitter looks after the children when we are out.
